samples.text:
The line graph shows the average age that men and women got married for the first time in one country from 1970 to 2020, and the bar chart shows how many marriages there was in the same period.

Overall, people married at older age over the period, but the number of marriages went down.

According to the line graph, in 1970 men married at 24.4 years and women at 22.4 years. The ages increased slowly until 1980, men was 25.3 and women 23.1. After that the ages rose faster. In 2000 men married at 29.9 and women at 27.8, and in 2020 the ages reached 33.8 for men and 31.9 for women. Men was always about two years older than women.

The bar chart shows that there were 415 thousand marriages in 1970. Then the number decreased every ten years. It was 370 thousand in 1980, 331 thousand in 1990 and 268 thousand in 2000. In 2010 it fell to 243 thousand and in 2020 there were only 196 thousand marriages, which is less than half of 1970.
samples.why: Clear but simple overview · both visuals covered accurately, though figures are listed rather than compared · basic linking (Then, After that) · adequate vocabulary · errors in agreement, articles and a comma splice.

samples.text:
The line graph illustrates changes in the average age at which men and women in a particular country first got married between 1970 and 2020, while the bar chart shows the total number of marriages over the same fifty years.

Overall, people married for the first time at an increasingly later age, with men consistently marrying about two years later than women. Meanwhile, the number of marriages decreased steadily throughout the period.

In 1970, the average age at first marriage was 24.4 for men and 22.4 for women. These figures rose only slightly over the following decade, but from 1980 onwards the increase became more rapid, with men reaching 29.9 and women 27.8 in 2000. By 2020, the average man was 33.8 when he first married, compared with 31.9 for women, meaning that both ages had risen by more than nine years.

Turning to the number of marriages, there were 415 thousand in 1970, and this figure fell in every decades shown. The sharpest drop took place in the 1990s, when numbers declined from 331 thousand to 268 thousand. By 2020 only 196 thousand couples married, which was less than half of the 1970 total.
samples.why: Clear overview of both trends and the constant gender gap · key features highlighted, including the sharpest fall · good cohesion · some less common expressions · one minor grammatical slip.

samples.text:
The line graph charts the average age at which men and women in one country entered their first marriage between 1970 and 2020, and the bar chart records the number of marriages across the same period.

Two clear trends emerge: first marriages took place progressively later in life for both sexes, and the number of marriages fell continuously, more than halving over the fifty years.

In 1970, men first married at an average age of 24.4 and women at 22.4. The rise was modest in the 1970s, but it accelerated markedly from 1980, and by 2020 the respective averages had reached 33.8 and 31.9, an increase of more than nine years for each sex. Notably, the gap between men and women remained remarkably consistent, at roughly two years, throughout the period.

Meanwhile, the number of marriages dropped from 415 thousand in 1970 to 331 thousand in 1990. The steepest fall came in the following decade, when the total declined by 63 thousand to 268 thousand. The downward trend continued into the twenty-first century, and by 2020 just 196 thousand marriages were recorded, fewer than half the number fifty years earlier.
samples.why: Concise, well-placed overview · key features and the stable gender gap selected skilfully · accurate derived figures · precise, natural vocabulary (progressively, respective) · wide range of structures with no errors.
